FN-HG5ZV83-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 381
Committee: State Government Sponsor: Representative David Faulkner
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 02/11/2026
House Bill 381 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Alabama Emergency
Management Agency (EMA) by an EMA-estimated $227,180 annually to issue emergency
preparedness licenses to camp operators, as well as (1) creating and maintaining a database
accessible to certain agencies with approved emergency plans from every camp; (2) maintaining
a list of camps with emergency preparedness licenses on the EMA website; (3) considering
applications and appeals and providing written explanations for denials of licenses; (4)
inspecting camps to verify compliance with the provisions of this bill; and (5) adopting rules
and regulations to administer the provisions of this bill.
This bill could also increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of Public Health,
Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, State Forestry Commission, Alabama
Department of Economic and Community Affairs, and the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency,
beginning in Fiscal Year 2026 and ending in Fiscal Year 2029, to reimburse their respective
members of the Youth Camp Safety Advisory Council for costs associated with attending
council meetings.

Economic Development

licenses on the EMA website; (3) considering applications and appeals and providing written
explanations for denials of licenses; (4) inspecting camps to verify compliance with the
provisions of this bill; and (5) adopting rules and regulations to administer the provisions of this
bill.
This bill could also increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of Public Health,
Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs, and the Alabama Law Enforcement
Agency, beginning in Fiscal Year 2026 and ending in Fiscal Year 2029, to reimburse their
respective members of the Youth Camp Safety Advisory Council for costs associated with
